# Open Peeps rights and provenance

Open Peeps is an official hand-drawn people illustration library by [Pablo Stanley](https://www.openpeeps.com/). The author’s page identifies the artwork as free for commercial and personal use under CC0 and says users may copy, modify, distribute, remix, and use it commercially without permission. The source page demonstrates mix-and-match vector parts, and links directly to SVG downloads for its bust, standing, and sitting example characters.

The page links to [CC0 1.0](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/) and to the author’s download listing. The release is identified as version 1.0 in [Pablo Stanley’s Open Peeps download listing](https://pablostanley.gumroad.com/l/openpeeps). No attribution is required. The standard CC0 deed is bundled in [CC0-1.0-LEGALCODE.txt](./CC0-1.0-LEGALCODE.txt).

## Included assets

- 80 original SVGs are kept under [`source/`](./source/).
- The exact official download URL, original file name, pose group, SHA-256, library identity, and catalog tags are recorded in [asset-manifest.json](./asset-manifest.json).
- Each Studio item links to the original Open Peeps CDN file and the author’s official rights page.
- Creator: Pablo Stanley.
- License: `CC0-1.0`, commercial use permitted, modifications and redistribution permitted, no attribution required.

We reviewed the official page’s 93 directly linked character examples as labeled contact sheets and omitted thirteen visually repetitive pose/outfit variants. The remaining 80 examples include bust, standing, and sitting poses. We preserved one figure with a wheelchair and tagged the feature shown in the artwork. The source does not provide character names, professions, ethnic identities, or individual file captions, so SweetOh does not infer them. Character art is tagged only by visible pose, people/portrait purpose, and supported design use.

The library contains drawings of people; CC0 does not grant publicity, privacy, or trademark rights in any recognizable real person or third-party marks. Users must not use an illustration to imply a person’s endorsement.
